facts.v: Preliminary Form S-1 registration statement filed May 20, 2026; the preliminary prospectus is subject to completion and share/price fields remain blank.
Space Exploration Technologies Corp., Texas corporation; principal executive offices at 1 Rocket Road, Starbase, Texas 78521.
Class A common stock has been applied for listing on Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas under “SPCX.”
Class A has one vote per share, Class B has ten votes per share, and Class C has no voting rights; Class B holders elect 51% of authorized directors.
The filing says the company will be a controlled company under Nasdaq/Nasdaq Texas rules and intends to rely on certain governance exemptions.
Financial statements are retrospectively recast for the xAI merger, X merger, and the five-for-one stock split effective May 4, 2026.
Net proceeds are planned for growth strategy: AI compute infrastructure, launch infrastructure and vehicles, satellite constellation scale/capacity, and general corporate purposes.
No cash dividends are anticipated for the foreseeable future; future earnings are expected to be retained for growth.
Filing fee exhibit registers Class A common stock under Rule 457(o) with a $1.0B maximum aggregate offering price and $138,100 net fee due.

segments.name: Space
segments.one_liner: Reusable rockets, spacecraft, launch services and mission services for internal and external payloads.
details: Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Dragon and Starship are the principal launch vehicles/spacecraft described in the filing.
Space segment revenue reflects customer launches and customer activities; internal Starlink deployment launches are capitalized in Connectivity, not recognized as Space revenue.
Starship is framed as the key enabler for V3 satellites, satellite-to-mobile, orbital AI compute, lunar and interplanetary objectives.

segments.name: Connectivity
segments.one_liner: Starlink broadband, enterprise, government/Starshield, and satellite-to-mobile services.
details: As of March 31, 2026, about 9,600 Starlink broadband/mobile satellites served about 10.3M subscribers across 164 countries, territories and other markets.
V1 Mobile satellites provided satellite-to-mobile data, over-the-top voice and messaging services to about 7.4M monthly unique devices across about 30 countries.
V3 satellites are designed for one Tbps downlink capacity per satellite and are expected to be deployed using Starship in H2 2026.

segments.name: AI
segments.one_liner: Grok, X, AI compute infrastructure, consumer/enterprise AI products and planned orbital AI compute.
details: xAI was acquired in early 2026 and is now described as an integral pillar of SpaceX.
COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II collectively provide about 1.0 GW of compute power; the first clusters came online in 122 days and 91 days, respectively.
Integrated Grok/X platforms had over 1.3B supported accounts active in the LTM ended March 31, 2026, about 550M MAUs and about 117M MAUs using Grok AI features.
